thread_text:
sara_support: FYI escalating — ACME (enterprise tier) reported a regression after today's canary. They say the model is now fabricating citations/URLs in responses that didn't exist before. Customer pasted multiple examples.

Dave_ACME: here are two verbatim outputs they got from our API: 
1) "According to Smith et al., 2025 (doi:10.000/xyz), the compound shows 78% yield." — we checked, Smith et al. 2025 with that DOI doesn't exist.
2) "See also: https://acme-research.org/papers/quant-2024" — this link 404s and the domain isn't ours.

sara_support: They say this was working fine with the previous model version (pinned to redwood-model-1.4) and only started after the rollout to redwood-model-2.0-canary (20% traffic). They attached request IDs for the calls and example prompts.

jason_se: thanks — can you paste one of the request IDs here? Also need model param, temp, and whether they used retrieval (RAG) or just the model.

Dave_ACME: request ids: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f, r-0f5e4d3c2b1a. Model header in their calls: "model: redwood-model-2.0". No explicit retrieval call from their side — they call our /v1/chat/completions. Prompt included: "Summarize the research on quantum catalysts and list three citations with links.". Temp=0.2, streaming=true.

liam_ml: digging into logs for those request ids. quick note: earlier today we changed the routing table so that for some enterprise accounts (including ACME) we now route to the cheaper 2.0-canary variant with a dynamic reranker enabled. Canary rollout started at 09:12 UTC.

opsbot: deploy event: canary rollout redwood-model-2.0-canary -> 20% traffic for enterprise cohort at 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z (initiated by emma_cs).

emma_cs: confirming — that was an ops decision to test performance improvements. We did not change system prompt content or the retrieval connector in that deploy.

jason_se: OK. two hypotheses: (1) model-2.0 has stronger tendency to produce plausible-sounding citations when RAG signals are absent/missing (hallucinated references), (2) reranker/db connector changed behavior causing empty search results but the generation path still fabricates citation fields. Need to reproduce locally.

liam_ml: repro steps I'm running: curl to /v1/chat/completions with the customer's prompt, model redwood-model-2.0-canary, temp 0.2, streaming off. I'll also toggle the reranker flag. Quick note — in logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e5f I see the retrieval step returned an empty hits array but downstream code still formatted a "sources" section by pulling placeholders from the search metadata (legacy fallback). That could explain fake links.

sara_support: can you paste the exact API request snippet we should run? I'll forward to ACME so they can repro on their side too.

liam_ml: sure — snippet: 
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, Model: redwood-model-2.0-canary
Body:
{
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the research on quantum catalysts and list three citations with links."}],
  "temperature": 0.2
}
```

jason_se: also capture the full response body including any "sources" or "citation" attributes. If it's RAG-enabled, there should be a non-empty hits array upstream. If upstream search is empty and generator is creating placeholder citations, that's a bug in the template/fallback logic.

emma_cs: checking monitoring — content-integrity alerts spiked right after the canary rollout: anomalies from 0.2/hr -> 3.7/hr for enterprise accounts in the last 3 hours. I've attached a quick metric screenshot.

Dave_ACME: here's one full response we saved (they redacted user PII): 
{
  "id": "r-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
  "model": "redwood-model-2.0-canary",
  "choices": [
    {
      "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Summary...
Sources:
1) Smith et al., 2025 — https://acme-research.org/papers/quant-2025
2) Johnson & Lee, 2023 — DOI:10.000/abc"}
    }
  ]
}

liam_ml: reproduced locally — with the reranker flag ON and an empty search response the generator inserts citation templates populated from leftover metadata placeholders (we have a legacy codepath that fills "author" and "url" from search metadata even when hits==[]). That code worked with older model because it rarely attempted to fill missing fields; model-2.0 apparently conditions more strongly on the "Sources:" token and invents plausible entries to match the template.

jason_se: that matches hypothesis. Immediate mitigations: 1) disable the legacy fallback that populates citation templates when hits==[]; 2) rollback routing for enterprise cohort to model-1.4; 3) patch generation prompt to include explicit "If you don't have verified sources, say "No verified sources found."".

emma_cs: I'm going to flip the routing for ACME and affected enterprise accounts back to model-1.4 right now (will take ~2 min).

deploy-bot: routing change executed: enterprise cohort restored to redwood-model-1.4 at 2026-03-15T11:02:58Z by emma_cs.

sara_support: ACME confirmed rollback fixed the problem for their sampled requests — no fabricated citations in 15 test calls. They still want an RCA and a timeline for a permanent fix.

liam_ml: I'll open a ticket on the codepath and push a hotfix to prevent template population on empty search results. Also adding a regression test that simulates empty-hits + model sampling to ensure no fabricated citations.

jason_se: also add a prompt-level guard: if retrieval_hits.length == 0, inject system message "Do not invent citations; reply that no verified sources are available.". We'll coordinate patch + canary re-roll.

sara_support: thanks team. Action items for customer-success: 1) send ACME the rollback confirmation and repro notes, 2) share ETA for hotfix and tests, 3) offer to run a private canary with them once the fix is verified.

Dave_ACME: appreciate the quick response. Please share when the fix is live and whether we need to flip anything on our side.

liam_ml: estimate for hotfix + tests + canary redeploy: ~6-8 hours. I'll update this thread when PR is merged.

sara_support: assigning follow-up to liam_ml and jason_se. tagging @dave_acme once we have an RCA doc. :white_check_mark:
